title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 39-41). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, lattice-theoretic framework (an 'atelier') with the following data.
- A: a set of objects (strata-like or cell-like elements).
- Σ_A: a lattice of 'supports', i.e. certain subsets of A, ordered by ≤ (inclusion), with an empty element ∅_Σ.
- Σcons_A ⊂ Σ_A: the 'constructible' supports. Page 39 notes that this class is in general stable neither under Sup, nor under Inf, nor under complement; an 'axiome des supports' replaces that compatibility.
- For X ∈ A, X° = supp°(X): the smallest S ∈ Σ_A with X ∈ S. This is read as 'the stratum associated with X'.
- A relation ≪ on A, presumably specialization, incidence or domination.
- For each X, an ordered set X̃, presumably the 'germs' or 'branches' of X; the image does not define it.

This page does two things.

(1) Programme. Grothendieck announces that he will now relate ≪, which has not yet been used, to the notion of support. He remarks that this nearly amounts to saying that the elements S ∈ Σ_A are ≪-closed subsets of A. So supports should be the closed sets of a specialization-type relation, as in a finite T0 / Alexandrov topology or the closure order of a stratification.

(2) The 'déploiement (spatial)' of X ∈ A. He defines Dep(X) = { X'° | X' ∈ X̃ } ⊂ Σcons ⊂ Σ. In words, the family of supports of the members of X̃. He notes that the definition would make sense for any F ∈ F(A), but restricts to X ∈ A. He then states four properties:
- (i) Dep(X) has a largest element, X°, and X° ≠ ∅_Σ.
- (ii) Its elements are mutually disjoint, written |·|.
- (iii) The map X̃ → Dep(X), X' ↦ X'°, is bijective.
- (iv) Dep(X) therefore inherits an order from X̃.

Grothendieck thus regards Dep(X) as a subset of Σ carrying an order relation. That is, an elementary set-theoretic 'figure' in Σ which is 'déployée', meaning its pieces are pairwise disjoint. Modern reading: Dep(X) is a finite poset of pairwise disjoint strata, a stratified 'picture' of X, much like the face poset of a cell or the strata of a local stratified model, with X° on top.

Use on the next page. If X ≪ Y, there is a canonical increasing map X̃ → Ỹ. It transports to an increasing ψ : Dep(X) → Dep(Y) with S ≤ ψ(S). ψ is unique because a nonempty S cannot lie below two distinct, hence disjoint, members of Dep(Y). This is exactly why disjointness (ii) is recorded here.

The problem served is a combinatorial or axiomatic theory of stratified objects and their incidence and specialization. It plausibly sits in the line of the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error is visible, but there is a potential ambiguity. 'Plus grand élément' X° must refer to the order transported from X̃, not to inclusion in Σ. Under inclusion, a largest element of a family of pairwise disjoint nonempty sets would force the family to be a singleton. The text resolves this only in the next sentence, where it says the order is inherited from X̃.
Assertions (i)-(iii) are stated without proof on this page. They presumably follow from axioms set out on earlier pages, which are not visible here, so they cannot be checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Supports (elements of Σ_A) as ≪-closed subsets of A: linking a specialization/incidence relation to a lattice of supports
ideas.modern_name: Closed sets of the specialization preorder (Alexandrov topology); closure-order of a stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937) for finite/Alexandrov spaces; folklore in stratification theory
ideas.where_published: Spirit related to Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology), but no such axiomatics is published there

ideas.what: Déploiement Dep(X): the ordered family of supports of the members of X̃, pairwise disjoint, with top element X°, in bijection with X̃
ideas.modern_name: Local stratified model / face poset of a cell viewed as a family of disjoint strata (exit-path/stratification poset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); face posets in combinatorial topology; exit-path categories (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie)
ideas.where_published: Apparently only in these unpublished 1986 'Ateliers' notes

ideas.what: Functoriality: X ≪ Y induces a unique increasing ψ: Dep(X) → Dep(Y) with S ≤ ψ(S), uniqueness coming from disjointness (completed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Induced map of stratification posets under specialization

missed.claim: The 'atelier' framework seems to be a purely lattice-theoretic or set-theoretic axiomatization of stratified objects. It works with supports, constructible supports, an 'axiome des supports', specialization ≪ and 'déploiements'. To my knowledge this framework is not in the literature and was never developed by others. This page holds one of its basic constructions: the ordered disjoint family Dep(X).
missed.quote: Dep(X) = {X'° | X' ∈ X̃} ⊂ Σcons ⊂ Σ ("déploiement" ("spatial") de X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may anticipate combinatorial or o-minimal-style axiomatics of stratified spaces and exit-path posets. Only historians of the 'topologie modérée' programme are likely to care; the construction itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary definitional step inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework as a whole is undocumented in the literature, but the content of this page (disjoint ordered family of supports, with uniqueness from disjointness) is routine.
transcription_corrections: '⊂ Σ_conv ⊂ Σ' should read '⊂ Σcons ⊂ Σ' (constructible supports, consistent with Σcons_A on p.39); likewise the struck-out subscript after 'de Σ' is 'cons', not 'conv'.
'($|0|$[?])' is the disjointness symbol '(|·|)', as used on p.41 ('T |·| T'').
The struck-out item in the set-builder is a crossed-out symbol before X'°; the superscript is ° (supp°), i.e. X'°, and 'X^0' should be read as X° throughout.
'(ce qui revient presque à dire ...)' is a parenthetical: 'au support, (ce qui revient presque à dire que les S ∈ Σ_A sont des parties ≪-fermées de A), à une notion de support.'
Last lines are roughly: 'Cela revient [à dire] [à considérer Dep X] comme une figure (élémentaire) ensembliste dans Σ, "déployée" i.e. les parties en sont deux à deux disjointes' (reading uncertain).
